title: A useful first conversation about your floor
summary: What to share before a home consultation, from room photos to the way you use your space.
sections: Start with the rooms

You do not need to have every decision made before speaking to FBS. Start with the rooms you want to change and why. A new home, an unfinished renovation and a single-room update can each need a different conversation. Tell the team which spaces are involved and whether anyone will be living in the property while work takes place.
Bring the information you already have

A floor plan, approximate room dimensions and a few photographs help explain the space. Include doorways, transitions to adjoining rooms and the existing floor. If you have chosen flooring elsewhere, share its specification and installation instructions. Photos are useful preparation, but they cannot confirm the condition of the surface beneath your floor.
Talk about your priorities

Let the team know what matters to you: the appearance, fitting approach, budget or a planned move. Explain any heating system or other practical requirement that needs to be reviewed. Be clear about the date you are aiming for, and whether it is a preference or linked to another trade.
Leave with a clear next step

Use the conversation to identify what needs to be assessed and what information is still missing. Ask what the fitting quotation will include, what you need to organise and how the next visit or appointment will be agreed. FBS offers a free home consultation; the work itself is agreed and quoted separately.

title: Measure your room. Start with a useful estimate.
summary: A simple way to estimate floor area before discussing the fitting work.
sections: Measure the space, not the furniture

For a rectangular room, measure the length and width in metres. Multiply the two measurements to estimate the floor area in square metres. For example, a room measuring 5 metres by 4 metres has an area of 20 m². Keep a note of the dimensions as well as the total so you can explain how you arrived at it.
Break an irregular room into sections

An L-shaped space is easier to understand as two rectangles. Sketch the shape, label each section and calculate each area separately. Add those areas together without counting an overlapping section twice. Door recesses and small alcoves can be easy to miss; mark them on your sketch rather than trying to hide them in a rough estimate.
Keep room totals separate

If you are planning several rooms, record each room individually. A room list helps the fitting team understand access, joins between spaces and the overall scope. Photographs and a floor plan can accompany the measurements. Do not use an approximate area as a substitute for a site assessment.
Use the result in your enquiry

Our room planner gives a rectangular-room estimate that you can add to your enquiry. The final measured area and fitting requirements should be reviewed with FBS. This estimate does not calculate a fitting price, material order quantity or cutting allowance; those depend on the details of the project.

title: Getting your room ready for floor fitting
summary: Questions to settle with your fitter before work starts, so everyone knows what to expect.
sections: Agree who is doing what

Before a fitting date is confirmed, discuss what needs to happen to the room. Ask who will move furniture, remove any existing floor and arrange disposal if those tasks are required. These are parts of the scope to agree, rather than assumptions to make. Tell the team about heavy furniture or items that cannot easily be moved.
Share the practical details

The existing surface, access to the room, door clearances and transitions to other floors may affect the work. Tell FBS about any known issue and share photographs where possible. A photo can show the layout but cannot establish whether a concealed surface is suitable for fitting.
Coordinate other work

If painting, kitchen fitting or other renovation work is happening, discuss the sequence with the people involved. Let FBS know which parts of the property are ready and which are still being worked on. A planned date should allow the space to be assessed and the fitting requirements to be agreed.
Confirm room readiness

Ask the fitting team for preparation instructions that suit your particular floor and project. The flooring manufacturer's instructions and the agreed fitting method matter. Check the arrangements for access, working areas and finishing details before the team arrives. Keep the quotation and any agreed preparation notes together so you can refer to them.

title: What to discuss about the surface beneath your floor
summary: Why the existing surface belongs in the fitting conversation, even when it is out of sight.
sections: Look beyond the finished surface

A new floor changes what you see, but the surface beneath it is part of the installation. Tell the fitting team whether the room has an existing covering, an exposed base or a surface that has recently been worked on. If you know how the current floor is constructed, include that information in your enquiry.
Describe what you have noticed

Mention movement, uneven areas or a known moisture issue. Avoid covering up a concern before it has been discussed. Photographs and a short description are useful ways to start the conversation, while a site assessment can identify what needs further review. FBS can discuss the fitting requirements for your space.
Ask what needs checking

The requirements depend on the exact flooring and fitting system. Ask how the existing surface will be assessed, what the manufacturer requires and whether preparation has been included in the scope. If the room has underfloor heating, tell the team about the system and provide any available specification.
Make preparation part of the quotation

If additional work is needed, ask for it to be described before fitting is agreed. Establish who will carry it out and how it affects the sequence of the project. Do not assume that a standard fitting quotation covers every possible condition beneath an existing floor. A clear scope helps everyone understand the next step.

title: What should your fitting quotation include?
summary: Compare the scope of the work, not just the number at the end of the quote.
sections: Describe the same project

A useful quotation starts with a clear description of the rooms and the work you are asking for. Share the approximate area, existing surface and the flooring specification if you already have it. If you are comparing quotations, make sure each conversation covers the same spaces and requirements.
Ask for the fitting scope

Request a description of the fitting work and any preparation that has been identified. Ask about transitions, edges and other finishing details that are relevant to your rooms. Check whether moving furniture, taking up an existing floor or waste disposal is included, excluded or still to be discussed.
Identify open questions

Some details may need a site assessment before they can be confirmed. Ask which parts of the quotation rely on assumptions and how additional work would be agreed if an issue is discovered. A quotation should help you see what has been planned and what still needs a decision.
Confirm timing and responsibilities

Discuss access, room readiness and the proposed sequence of work. Ask how the fitting date will be confirmed and what you need to do beforehand. This website does not publish fixed fitting rates: the price depends on the work agreed for your project. Contact FBS to discuss your requirements and request a quotation.

title: Plan the flooring stage in your new home
summary: Bring the floor plan, explain your move-in plans and coordinate the next steps.
sections: Begin with the floor plan

A plan helps explain the rooms and the way they connect. Tell FBS which spaces need fitting and whether the project will be completed together or in stages. Add any approximate measurements you have, while keeping in mind that the space still needs to be reviewed.
Share the handover information

Let the team know your planned handover and move-in dates. Explain which dates are confirmed and which are still changing. If you are waiting for access to the property, say so at the first conversation. This helps the team identify when an assessment and the fitting stage can be discussed.
Connect the trades

Floor fitting is one part of finishing a home. Share information about other work happening in the property so the sequence can be reviewed with the people involved. Tell the fitting team about the existing base, heating system and anything the builder has provided about the space.
Agree the work before the date

A target date is helpful, but it is not a confirmed booking. Review the room readiness, fitting scope and any preparation requirements with FBS first. Keep a note of who is responsible for each task. FBS offers consultation and fitting for new-home projects; contact the team to discuss the next step for yours.

title: Doorways, edges and the finishing conversation
summary: Small details worth discussing before the fitting scope is agreed.
sections: Walk through the connections

Flooring does not end in the middle of a room. Show the fitting team how the space connects to hallways, doorways and adjoining surfaces. Include these areas in your photographs and measurements. A change in floor level or material is useful information to share early.
Discuss the edges

The details around the perimeter affect the finished appearance. Ask which approach is suitable for your floor and what work is included. Existing skirting, fixed furniture and door frames may need to be considered alongside the flooring system. Avoid assuming that one finishing method works for every installation.
Check the doors

Tell FBS about doors that currently catch the floor or have little clearance. The height of the proposed flooring system may be relevant to the fitting plan. Ask how any door-related work will be assessed and whether it is part of the agreed quotation.
Make the details visible in the scope

Use the consultation to identify the transitions and finishing requirements for each room. Ask what is included and what still needs to be confirmed. The right detail depends on the exact floor, surrounding surfaces and installation instructions. Agree those decisions with the fitting team before work begins.

title: Already have your flooring? Prepare for fitting.
summary: Share the specification and follow the right storage and preparation instructions.
sections: Send the specification first

If you already have flooring, tell FBS what it is before agreeing fitting. Share the manufacturer, exact specification and installation instructions. Include the condition of the materials and whether they have already been delivered. The team needs that information to review the fitting requirements for your rooms.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions

Storage and acclimatisation requirements vary between flooring systems. Use the instructions supplied for the exact material rather than a generic rule from another installation. Ask the fitting team if any instruction is unclear, and explain how and where the flooring has been stored.
Keep the space in the conversation

The rooms, existing base and any heating system matter alongside the material. Share photographs and any information you have about the current surface. If the property is still being renovated or has only recently become accessible, explain that at the first conversation.
Check what is needed next

Before the fitting date is agreed, confirm the preparation instructions and who is responsible for each task. Ask the fitter to review the material requirements and scope for your project. Contacting FBS does not confirm a fitting booking; the team will discuss suitability, room readiness and availability with you.
